title: Road Trip Cost Calculator: Fuel and Splits
description: Route a road trip on real roads and price its fuel with the Road Trip Cost Calculator — total cost and the split per person. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 640-mile round trip at 30 mpg and $3.60 a gallon burns 21.3 gallons and costs $76.80 — $19.20 each for four friends, computed before anyone argues.
quick_answer: The Road Trip Cost Calculator routes your journey on real roads, applies your car's fuel economy and your price, and returns the fuel needed, the total cost and the split per person. Add the start, stops and destination, set the economy and price, and read the cost before the trip.

faq: Where does the fuel price come from?
From you. Enter the price you actually pay (or the route's typical price) — the calculator applies it, it never fetches or invents one.
Is the distance the real road distance?
Yes — the route is built on the road network, so the miles priced are the miles driven.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Traffic barely moves fuel cost at trip scale; your real-world economy figure absorbs it.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Roads wind — and this calculator prices the road figure, which is the one your tank will meet.
Can route results change over time?
Distances are stable; prices are not. Re-run with the current price when the trip is near.
Can it split unevenly?
The built-in split is even. Uneven shares (driver exempt, part-way riders) are the Fuel Cost Split Calculator's per-leg craft.
Round trip or one-way?
Route what you will drive — add the return as the final leg, or run the pair as a round trip, and the price covers it.
Electric road trips?
The structure survives with kWh and charger prices, but this page is built for fuel by name and inputs — the EV tools elsewhere frame range; the cost arithmetic here assumes a pump.
Why not include tolls automatically?
Tolls depend on the exact roads and payment methods; the calculator prices what it can compute honestly and leaves tolls to your route check.
Can I run it for one person?
Yes — the split becomes the total, which is the solo traveller's whole budget line for fuel.
